name: How do I make a small bathroom look larger during a remodel?

mainEntity.name: How do I make a small bathroom look larger during a remodel without moving walls?
mainEntity.text: How do I make a small bathroom look larger during a remodel without moving walls?

acceptedAnswer.text: A small bathroom can feel much larger without moving walls if the remodel is designed around visual openness and efficient storage. Lighter finishes, larger-format tile, frameless shower glass, wall-mounted fixtures, and layered lighting all reduce visual clutter. Limiting the number of materials and grout lines can also make the room feel calmer and more expansive. Storage should be built in where possible so countertops stay clear. In a compact Los Angeles bathroom, these choices often deliver a bigger impact than a structural change. The best results come from combining design tricks with practical function, such as improving the shower entrance, increasing mirror size, and selecting a vanity that fits the room proportionally. If you want the room to appear more spacious, ask your contractor or designer to show how each finish choice affects the perception of size, not just the budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Use a lighter color palette, larger-format tile, frameless glass, better lighting, and fewer visual breaks to make a small bathroom feel larger. A cleaner layout and better storage also improve openness without changing the room’s footprint.
